holidays.name: Pocky & Presto Day
holidays.description: A snack celebration in Japan and beyond where people exchange long, skinny biscuit sticks coated in chocolate. The date 11/11 looks like four sticks standing in a row, so fans snack in formation.
holidays.origin: Glico, the Japanese confectioner behind Pocky, registered November 11 as Pocky Day in 1999, since the numerals 1111 resemble the sticks.
holidays.funFact: Pocky was introduced in 1966, and in some countries it is sold as Mikado. The name comes from the Japanese onomatopoeia 'poki,' the sound of snapping a stick.

holidays.name: Singles' Day (Guanggun Jie)
holidays.description: A holiday that began as a celebration of being single and has grown into the biggest online shopping event on Earth. People treat themselves to discounts, gifts, and plenty of 'self-love' purchases.
holidays.origin: It began in the 1990s among students at Nanjing University, who picked 11/11 because the four 1s look like 'bare sticks,' or single people. Alibaba turned it into a shopping festival in 2009.
holidays.funFact: Singles' Day sales have reached tens of billions of dollars in a single day, dwarfing Black Friday and Cyber Monday combined by some measures.

holidays.name: Origami Day
holidays.description: A day for folding paper into cranes, frogs, and fancy boxes, with an unreasonable number of paper cuts as the price of admission.
holidays.origin: Observed in Japan and among paper-folding enthusiasts, it was linked to November 11 partly because of the date's tidy straight-line look and the long tradition of the art of 'ori' (folding) and 'kami' (paper).
holidays.funFact: A traditional goal in Japan is folding 1,000 paper cranes, called senbazuru, which legend says earns the folder a wish.

holidays.name: Sundae Day
holidays.description: A day for piling ice cream, syrup, whipped cream, nuts, and a cherry into a glorious dish of dessert indulgence. Eating the cherry first is considered a bold strategic choice.
holidays.origin: National Sundae Day is celebrated in the US in the fall, with November 11 observed in some years by dessert fans. The sundae itself has disputed roots, with Ithaca, New York, and Two Rivers, Wisconsin, both claiming to have invented it in the 1890s.
holidays.funFact: One popular theory says the dish was spelled 'sundae' to avoid offending religious sensibilities about serving a treat called a 'Sunday.'

holidays.name: Veterans Day Quirk: The 11th Hour Moment of Silence
holidays.description: Beyond the parades, many places observe a quiet moment at 11:11 a.m., marking the instant the World War I armistice took effect. It is a solemn tradition with a peculiar numeric symmetry.
holidays.origin: The armistice that ended fighting in World War I took effect at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month in 1918, and Armistice Day later became Veterans Day in the US and Remembrance Day in the Commonwealth.
holidays.funFact: The red poppy became the symbol of Remembrance Day thanks to the poem 'In Flanders Fields,' and poppies were among the first flowers to bloom on churned-up battlefields.
